description_full: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. discovers, invents, develops, manufactures, and commercializes medicines to treat various diseases worldwide. The company develops product candidates to treat eye, allergic and inflammatory, cardiovascular, metabolic, neurological, infectious, and rare diseases; and cancer, hematologic conditions. It also offers EYLEA injections for wet age-related macular degeneration and diabetic macular edema; myopic choroidal neovascularization; diabetic retinopathy; neovascular glaucoma; retinopathy of prematurity; Dupixent injection to treat atopic dermatitis and asthma; Libtayo injection for metastatic or locally advanced cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma; Praluent injection to treat heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH); and Kevzara solution for rheumatoid arthritis. It has license and collaboration agreement with Bayer for the development and commercialization of EYLEA 8 mg and EYLEA; Alnylam Pharmaceuticals, Inc. to discover, develop, and commercialize RNAi therapeutics for diseases by addressing therapeutic disease targets expressed in eye and central nervous system; Intellia Therapeutics, Inc. to advance CRISPR/Cas9 gene-editing technology for in vivo therapeutic development for therapies focused on neurological and muscular diseases; Hansoh Pharmaceuticals Group Company Limited to acquire development and commercial rights for HS-20094, a dual GLP-1/GIP receptor; and Tessera Therapeutics, Inc. develops and commercializes TSRA-196, an investigational gene editing therapy for Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency. The company has a strategic collaboration with Telix Pharmaceuticals Limited to develop and commercialize radiopharmaceutical therapies. It also has a strategic collaboration with CytomX Therapeutics, Inc. to create conditionally-activated bispecific cancer therapies. It has a strategic alliance with Sanofi to develop long-acting immunology antibodies. The company was incorporated in 1988 and is based in Tarrytown, New York.

financial_summary: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. is a large-cap healthcare business with a $98.8B market cap on $14.3B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +6% over the past three years and +13% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size. Operating margins are expanding by +3.1pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 22% against a 8% cost of capital — a 14-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $4.1B in free cash flow — roughly 28 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.11× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 82× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 3.2% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 2.1% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 2.8× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 54% above its 10-year median.

prof: ROIC of 22% clears the cost of capital of 8.3% by 14pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.76).
It converts 28% of revenue into free cash flow, or 22% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.11x.
ROE of 14% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.3x equity multiplier).

hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $6.6B (7% of market cap).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 5.6% over 3 years, 11.0% over 5 years and 13.3% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 54%).

Free cash flow has compounded 15.3% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: deferred revenue down 6% and 113 active clinical trials.
Capex runs 1.7x depreciation (6.3% of sales), so it is building capacity for future growth.
own: Insiders own a modest 2.1%, and institutions hold 93%.

It returns 3.2% a year to shareholders (2.8% in buybacks and 0.4% in dividends).

people: With about 15,410 employees, each generates about $931K of revenue, 2.5x the Healthcare median, and revenue has grown 25.8% a year across its filed history.

The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
